01 · The list

Feelings,
level by level

Words for feelings in Korean: happy, sad, angry, tired, surprised, to like and to worry, and the other states of mind on the TOPIK vocabulary lists, each with its reading and meaning.

In Lock&Learn Korean these words sit in their level packs (Beginner 1, Beginner 2, Advanced 1), one per glance on the widget: a word waits in hangul with its romanization; one tap reveals the meaning and a real sentence. Beginner 1 is free; every other pack opens with a free preview and another word unlocks daily.

Type to filter by hangul, romanization or meaning. Flashcards hides the meaning until you tap a row; Shuffle deals the list in a new order.

03 · Questions

Asked and
answered

How do I express feelings in Korean?

The 41 words below are the emotion and feeling words on the TOPIK vocabulary lists with their readings and meanings. The beginner-level entries come with a real sentence.

Which TOPIK levels are these words from?

40 from TOPIK I, 1 from TOPIK II Advanced. The level chip on each row says where the word sits, so you can stop at your level or read ahead. Beginner-level words carry a real example sentence; the rest show word, romanization and meaning, with their sentences in the app.

How do I learn feelings words on my iPhone Lock Screen?

Install Lock&Learn Korean, then touch and hold your Lock Screen, tap Customize, tap the widget area and choose Lock&Learn Korean. Enable the level packs these words come from (Beginner 1, Beginner 2, Advanced 1). A word waits in hangul with its romanization; one tap reveals the meaning and a real sentence.

Is Lock&Learn Korean free?

Yes. The app is free on iOS: Beginner 1 is free, every other pack opens with a free preview, and another word unlocks daily. Lock&Learn+ is an optional upgrade that opens every pack at once, offered as a yearly plan or a one-time lifetime purchase.
